paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Isaiah 20 is about where you put your hope. The people of the coastland had run to Egypt and Cush for help against Assyria, and the LORD sent a walking, barefoot sign to say that hope was going to let them down. Egypt and Cush were the ones they "made… their hope," and Isaiah 20:5 says those who did will be "dismayed and ashamed."

Now, I know a thing or two about trusting something that looks solid. I once figured a shiny new stamper on the counter meant my whole future was set, and then it was just a different drawer for somebody else. Hope in a big, impressive thing feels safe right up until the day it can't carry you. Look at the question in verse 6: "How then can we escape?" They only asked it once the thing they trusted was gone.

So take it home, baker. Ask yourself what you're running to when the pressure hits: your savings, your connections, your plan, your own strength. None of those are bad to have, but none of them were made to be your rescue. Put your whole weight on the LORD, because He's the only One who won't leave you asking that question.
